slides.title: Browser Session
slides.subtitle: Join the agent's own browser to its Session with a one-time code and a proof
slides.notes: PAP can carry one Session across APIs, conversations and the company's website. This example shows how the browser the agent controls joins the Session the agent already has: through a form on the company's browser-session page, a one-time code, and a DPoP proof signed with the Session Key.

slides.title: Why a Browser Session
slides.statement: One Session, on the **API** and on the **website**: the same user, the same sign-in, the same scopes.
slides.notes: Sometimes the agent needs a company web page, say to confirm an operation. Instead of signing in again, the browser joins the Session the agent already holds, signed in or out.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Your host, trusted"] direction TB A["Personal agent"] -- "read the code" --> B["Agent's own browser
not the user's"] A -- "sign over the code" --> D["Reactor DPoP provider
holds the Session Key"] end subgraph CO["Company"] direction TB E["Browser-session endpoint
form, then cookie"] -- "code used once" --> R[("Join codes")] end HOST -- "GET, then code and proof" --> CO HOST -. "statuses, booleans" .-> M
slides.caption: The code comes from the company's page in the agent's own browser; the model gets statuses and yes-or-no evidence.
slides.notes: Inside the host, the personal agent has its own browser, not the user's ordinary browser, load the company's browser-session endpoint, the one discovery advertised. The page holds a one-time code. The host reads it from that page alone and has the Reactor DPoP provider sign a proof over it with the Session Key. The browser posts code and proof back; the company uses the code once, checks the proof, and answers 303 with its own cookie for the Session. Off to the side, the model receives statuses and yes-or-no evidence, never the code, the proof or the cookie.

slides.title: Joining the Session

items.title: Load
items.detail: GET the endpoint: a form with a one-time code

items.title: Tie
items.detail: A __Host- SameSite=Strict cookie binds code to browser

items.title: Sign
items.detail: DPoP proof with the Session Key; the code as nonce

items.title: Submit
items.detail: The browser posts code and proof

slides.notes: The browser loads the endpoint with a GET as a top-level navigation. The page is a form with a hidden code of at least 128 random bits, valid for 60 seconds at most, and an empty proof field; a __Host- cookie, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, ties the code to this browser. The agent signs a DPoP proof with the Session Key: htm POST, htu the endpoint, the code as nonce, no ath. The browser submits the form; the company answers 303 with its own cookie for the Session.

slides.title: Agent responsibilities
items: Join only at the advertised HTTPS `web.browser_session_endpoint`
Read the code from the page **its own browser** loaded, nowhere else
Sign with the Session Key of the Session the browser joins
Proof: `htm` POST, `htu` the endpoint, `nonce` the code, no `ath`
Read and sign in host code the model cannot read
slides.notes: BrowserSessionClient resolves the clock, the DPoP provider and the browser through Reactor: pap.browserJoin loads the form and submits it. A code from a message, a conversation or another page may come from someone else's browser, which would then join the user's Session; so the code comes only from the page the agent's own browser loaded.

slides.title: Join once, refuse the rest
slides.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Agent's browser
  participant C as Company endpoint
  participant X as Another browser
  B->>C: GET the join page
  C-->>B: Form with code, join cookie
  B->>C: POST code and proof, with cookie
  C->>C: Cookie, code, proof, Session Key
  C-->>B: 303 and Session cookie
  B->>C: Same code again
  C-->>B: 400, code already used
  X->>C: Fresh code, no join cookie
  C-->>X: 400, and the code is used up
slides.notes: Follow the first POST. The company checks that the join cookie matches the code, that the code is one it issued, unexpired and unused, that the proof is valid for this POST with the code as nonce, and that its key is an active Session's key; an unknown key is an error here, never a new Session. The first use goes through: 303 with the company's cookie. The same code again, even with a fresh valid proof, is refused: a code is used by the first request that sends it. A fresh code submitted from another browser, without the join cookie, is refused too, and is used up.

slides.title: The company's cookie
slides.statement: `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, set only on the join, and it **never outlives** the PAP Session.
slides.notes: The cookie follows later sign-in, sign-out and scope changes. In the reference companies, the __Host-poppy_session cookie has no lifetime of its own, so signing out reaches the website on its next request. Joining again replaces it.

slides.title: What stays where

left.heading: Never in a URL or model context
items: The proof and the Session Key

slides.notes: The code and the proof travel only in the form body, from the agent's own browser. What the model gets back is the status of each step and yes-or-no evidence that each rule held.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI example joins against the reference company, then replays a code and submits one from another browser, and sees both refused
slides.notes: The example runs Manzanita with its website on, in one process. It joins the agent's own browser through a Reactor pap.browserJoin contribution, checks the proof's key and nonce, then tries a replayed code and a code from another browser. Upstream's Web browsing section has the rules in full.
